Judge: A wins all four pairs clearly, and none is close. The A frames show premium character fidelity: real skin detail, readable hands and weapons, and cloth with seams and folds. They have believable materials (clear-coat and chrome reflections, metal speculars, weathered surfaces), atmospheric lighting (the moonlit, stained-glass night in pair 1 is the standout) and deliberate cinematic framing. The B frames share the same failures in every pair. Characters show blocky posterized or dithered shading on skin, hair and cloth, worst on the arms and hands at close range. Pistols render as shapeless black blobs. The muzzle flash is a horizontal smear with speed-lines. Materials are flat and diffuse, with no reflections on cars or glass. There are placeholder props: blank green signs, a white-frame/blue-wheel cluster in the centre of the sidewalk, and an empty-grid minimap. The HUD is heavy and has a garbled text string, and the framing is awkward, with figures cut off and the crosshair over the hero's own hands. B's genuine strengths are warm golden-hour light, a recognisable location (landmark skyline, shophouses, hawker centre) and a believable crowd density in the food centre. The fastest wins for B are close-range character and weapon shading, then removing placeholder props and adding reflective material response on vehicles. Blinding note: two A frames carry a publisher logo watermark and every B frame has a gameplay HUD, so it was possible to infer which image came from which source. Stripping both from future pairs would make the test fairer. These verdicts rest on visual merit and would not change if the HUD and watermarks were removed.
